claims.excerpt: This was Tom Allen, British-born, former champion of the world

claims.statement: Tom Allen was a cold-eyed Englishman of about 170 pounds and lately champion around 1873.
claims.excerpt: There was Tom Allen, a cold-eyed Englishman of 170 pounds, lately champion

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost the world heavyweight title to Mike McCoole on a foul in 1869, after thugs cut the ropes and intimidated the referee.
claims.excerpt: had cut the ropes when it was certain McCoole could not win, intimidating the referee into declaring McCoole victor on a foul

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Mike McCoole in seven rounds on Chouteau Island on September 23, 1873, regaining the world heavyweight title.
claims.excerpt: The end came in the seventh round with Mike virtually blind in both eyes

claims.statement: The article says Tom Allen was the only man in heavyweight championship history to lose his title and regain it.
claims.excerpt: the only man in the history of the heavyweight championship to lose his title and regain it

claims.statement: Mike McCoole loaned Tom Allen $200 to cover Allen's share of the $1,000 side bet placed with referee John Looney before the 1873 fight.
claims.excerpt: McCoole, when he found Allen had only $800 cash to cover his own $1000, loaned Allen the extra $200

claims.statement: Johnny Daly was Tom Allen's handler at the 1873 fight with Mike McCoole.
claims.excerpt: He asked his handler, Johnny Daly, for a file

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost his world title to Joe Goss in a fight near Louisville, Kentucky, three years after the 1873 McCoole fight.
claims.excerpt: Allen, three years later, had his title wrested from him in a desperate struggle near Louisville by Joe Goss

claims.statement: After losing his title, Tom Allen retired to his public house.
claims.excerpt: Allen soon retired to his public house, where he continued to be a factor

claims.statement: Tom Allen's saloon was called the Champion's Rest and kept running in a milder way until the day of his death.
claims.excerpt: continued to function in a milder way, strictly in an Allenesque manner, to the day of his demise

claims.statement: Tom Allen's saloon was on Market Street, east of Seventh Street, in St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: Allen's place was on Market, east of Seventh
places: Market Street, east of Seventh Street, St. Louis

claims.excerpt: right down to his death in 1905

claims.statement: Tom Allen backed Artie Flint in Flint's fight against Hugh McManus near St. Clair, Missouri, on April 16, 1888.
claims.excerpt: since old Tom was back of Flint and Tom Kelly, who seconded McCoole in the old days, was in McManus' corner
places: six miles from St. Clair, Missouri

claims.statement: The day after the Flint fight, a Post-Dispatch reporter interviewed Tom Allen at his saloon.
claims.excerpt: The next day, in his saloon, the Post-Dispatch reporter interviewed Allen.

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: Tom, it's a bloody shame to put such a man up before me—take him out.
quotes.topic: urging Kelly to stop the McCoole fight

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: no title, decided under any other than London prize-ring rules, with the 'raw 'uns,'
quotes.topic: against gloves and the Queensberry code

fights.notes: Only mentioned in passing; no place, rounds or rules given. Result was a foul.

fights.excerpt: The end came in the seventh round with Mike virtually blind in both eyes
fights.notes: Retrospective account from 1928. The 16 minutes includes the 30-second intermissions.

notes: 1928 retrospective; Flint 1888 and Kelly/Daly material is about others but Allen is named in each. Dates for 1869 and 1876 are approximate from passing mentions.
